briefdescription.para: Computes the I3C odd-parity bit for a 7-bit dynamic address.

detaileddescription.para: Per the I3C spec and the DEV_ADDR_TABLE_LOC*n*.DEV_DYNAMIC_ADDR field, bit[7] of the 8-bit encoded value must be the odd parity of bits[6:0], that is, parity = ~XOR(addr[6:0]). The controller transmits this 8-bit value verbatim during ENTDAA, so a raw address write with bit[7]=0 produces wrong parity for any 7-bit address that has an even number of 1-bits (for example 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0C, 0x0F, 0x11, 0x12, ...) and the slave NACKs the address assignment, hanging the controller.

parameterdescription.para: The 7-bit dynamic address (only bits[6:0] are used).

simplesect.para: 0 or 1 - the odd-parity bit to place in bit[7].

briefdescription.para: Brings the controller back to a usable state after a transfer error.

detaileddescription.para: An error response such as a receive buffer overflow leaves the core halted, and it stays halted until RESUME is written. The FIFOs are cleared after that because a transfer aborted part way through can leave untransmitted data behind in the TX FIFO.
This does not restore a target that has latched an error into its CCC_DEVICE_STATUS; that register is read only and needs the controller to read it with GETSTATUS.

simplesect.para: RESUME must be written before the FIFOs are reset. Resetting the FIFOs of a halted core leaves it halted.

briefdescription.para: Initiates a polled mode send in master mode.

detaileddescription.para: It sends data to the FIFO and waits for the slave to pick them up. If master fails to send data due arbitration lost, stops the transfer and with arbitration lost status If slave fails to remove data from FIFO, the send fails with time out.

parameterdescription.para: The number of bytes to be sent.

simplesect.para: This send routine is for polled mode transfer only. All the FIFO operations are in terms of words.

briefdescription.para: Initiates a polled mode receive in master mode.

detaileddescription.para: It repeatedly sets the transfer size register so the slave can send data to us. It polls the data register for data to come in. If master fails to read data due arbitration lost, returns with arbitration lost status. If slave fails to send us data, it fails with time out.

parameterdescription.para: The number of bytes to be received.

simplesect.para: This receive routine is for polled mode transfer only.

detaileddescription.para: It does the protocol handling for the interrupt-driven transfers.

If the Master is receiving data then the data is read from the FIFO and the Master has to request for more data (if there is more data to receive). If all the data has been received then a completion event is signalled to the upper layer by calling the callback handler. It is an error if the amount of received data is more than expected.
The driver calls the handler from interrupt context when an In-Band Interrupt is received from a target.

parameterdescription.para: The upper-layer callback reference, passed back to the handler when it is invoked.
Pointer to the IBI callback function.

simplesect.para: The handler runs in interrupt context and must copy the payload out immediately; the payload buffer is reused on the next IBI.

briefdescription.para: Enables In-Band Interrupt (SIR) reception for a single target.

detaileddescription.para: It clears the SIR reject in the target's DAT entry and in the global reject register, sets IBI-with-data if the target's BCR advertises a mandatory data byte, lazily enables the IBI threshold interrupt, and sends ENEC(SIR) to the target.

parameterdescription.para: The Device Address Table index of the target (same index used during dynamic address assignment).

listitem.para: XST_SEND_ERROR if the ENEC(SIR) payload could not be sent.
XST_TIMEOUT if the IBI queue reset or the ENEC(SIR) response never completed.

briefdescription.para: Disables In-Band Interrupt (SIR) reception for a single target.

detaileddescription.para: It sends DISEC(SIR) to the target, sets the SIR reject in both the DAT entry and the global reject register, and disables the IBI threshold interrupt if no targets remain armed.

parameterdescription.para: The Device Address Table index of the target.

listitem.para: XST_SEND_ERROR if the DISEC(SIR) payload could not be sent.
XST_TIMEOUT if the DISEC(SIR) response never completed.

detaileddescription.para: The driver calls the handler from interrupt context to flag a Hot-Join request. The joining target is NOT yet enrolled when the handler runs; the application must run enrolment (ENTDAA) via XI3cPsx_HotJoinDaa() from thread context.

parameterdescription.para: The upper-layer callback reference, passed back to the handler when it is invoked.
Pointer to the Hot-Join callback function.

simplesect.para: The handler runs in interrupt context, so its work should be minimized (for example record the event and return).

detaileddescription.para: It clears DEVICE_CTRL.HOT_JOIN_CTRL so the controller ACKs a Hot-Join request, and lazily enables the IBI threshold interrupt (shared with SIR) since Hot-Join requests are reported through the same IBI queue.

simplesect.para: A Hot-Join sets HotJoinPending and invokes the Hot-Join handler from the ISR. The blocking ENTDAA enrolment is deferred: the application must call XI3cPsx_HotJoinDaa() from thread context to assign the new target its dynamic address.

detaileddescription.para: It sets DEVICE_CTRL.HOT_JOIN_CTRL so the controller NACKs a Hot-Join request, and disables the IBI threshold interrupt if no SIR target remains armed either.

briefdescription.para: Services a Hot-Join request by re-running ENTDAA.

detaileddescription.para: Services a Hot-Join request by re-running ENTDAA (without RSTDAA, so existing targets keep their address) and refreshing the captured BCR of every enumerated target on success.

simplesect.para: Must be called from thread (non-interrupt) context - for example from the application after a Hot-Join notification. The ISR only flags the Hot-Join via HotJoinPending. The ENTDAA is issued interrupt-driven so the live ISR is the single response consumer; a polled send would race the ISR (which clears the response first) and time out.

briefdescription.para: Receives a buffer in polled mode as a slave.

simplesect.para: This receive routine is for polled mode transfer only. All the FIFO operations are in terms of words, so MsgPtr must hold a word rounded count. The number of bytes received is reported in CurrByteCount.

detaileddescription.para: It does the protocol handling for the interrupt-driven transfers.
Completion events and errors are signaled to upper layer for proper handling.

The interrupts that are handled are:
DATA If the instance is sending, it means that the master wants to read more data from us. Send more data, and check whether we are done with this send.
If the instance is receiving, it means that the master has written more data to us. Receive more data, and check whether we are done with with this receive.
COMP This marks that stop sequence has been sent from the master, transfer is about to terminate. However, for receiving, the master may have written us some data, so receive that first.
It is an error if the amount of transferred data is less than expected.
NAK This marks that master does not want our data. It is for send only.
Other interrupts These interrupts are marked as error.

briefdescription.para: Implements the PS I3C driver for master and slave transfers.

detaileddescription.para: This is an implementation of I3C driver in the PS block. The device can be either a master or a slave on the I3C bus. This implementation supports both interrupt mode transfer and polled mode transfer.
The higher level software must implement a higher layer protocol to inform the slave what to send to the master.
The XI3cPsx_Config structure is used by the driver to configure itself. This configuration structure is typically created by the tool-chain based on HW build properties.
To support multiple runtime loading and initialization strategies employed by various operating systems, the driver instance can be initialized in the following way:

listitem.para: XI3cPsx_LookupConfig(DeviceId) - Use the device identifier to find the static configuration structure defined in XI3cPsx_g.c. This is setup by the tools. For some operating systems the config structure is initialized by the software and this call is not needed.

XI3cPsx_CfgInitialize(InstancePtr, CfgPtr, EffectiveAddr) - Uses a configuration structure provided by the caller. If running in a system with address translation, the provided virtual memory base address replaces the physical address in the configuration structure.

detaileddescription.para: Multiple slaves are supported by selecting them with unique addresses.
This driver supports polled mode transfers.

The application must connect the interrupt handler of the driver, XI3cPsx_InterruptHandler to an interrupt system such that it is called when an interrupt occurs. This function does not save and restore the processor context such that the application must provide this processing.

The driver handles the following interrupts:
Transfer complete
More Data
Error
